observation.visible_scene: A clear acrylic stand on a wooden table holds a vertically mounted metal/plastic spiral coil (concentric circles) centered on a small pivot. A bright blue rod-like object is attached at the pivot and is seen in every frame as a blurred radial streak pointing in a different direction, indicating it is spinning about the vertical axis. A thin white curved arc also appears around the coil and shifts its orientation from frame to frame. The background is a black panel with a gray wall at the right; the camera is static (stand, base, and background do not translate). In the first several frames a person's sleeve and blurred hand/arm are visible at the left edge, then withdraw out of view while the blue object keeps sweeping.
visible_changes: The blue rod's blurred streak rotates continuously about the central pivot, cycling through left -> up-left -> up -> right -> down-right -> down -> left repeatedly across the excerpt (a full revolution every ~0.4 s by the sampled frames).
The thin white arc changes its angular position around the coil in step with the rotation, sweeping clockwise as well.

The person's hand/arm at the left edge moves progressively out of frame: present and blurred near the top-left and bottom-left in frames 1-8, reduced to a blurred hand in frame 8, and absent (only the sleeve edge remains) from frame 9 onward.
The concentric spiral coil, the clear support posts, the white base plate, the green mat and the wooden board remain fixed in position and size throughout (no translation or scaling).
The blue object's blur length and orientation change frame to frame, but it always radiates from the central pivot (rotation about a fixed point, not translation of the whole device).
outside_clip_unknowns: What set the blue rod spinning (no contact is shown within the excerpt; the hand is already withdrawn by mid-clip).
Whether the rotation continues, slows, or stops after the last frame.
The identity/purpose of the device and the exact material of the blue object.
What happened before t=0 (the spin was already underway at the first frame).
uncertain_details: Whether the spiral coil itself rotates or is stationary (its concentric shape looks the same either way; only the white arc's motion is visible).
Whether the white arc is a fixed outer end of the coil, a separate wire, or a motion-blur trail of the blue rod's tip.
Exact rotation direction and angular speed, since heavy motion blur and the ~15 Hz sampling cause aliasing; the clockwise reading is the most consistent but not guaranteed.
Whether the hand's withdrawal is causally linked to the spin or simply the operator stepping back after an unseen start.

trace.prompt:
Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
These are chronological samples of a TEMPORALLY CROPPED SEGMENT of a longer source video.
Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
